title: Winners and losers of NBA's first week: Giannis' Heat are ice cold, OKC injuries and new-look wonders - CBS Sports
description: Tracking the first night of the NBA season is pretty straightforward. Every game occupies a single broadcast window. True opening night,
body:
Tracking the first night of the NBA season is pretty straightforward. Every game occupies a single broadcast window. True opening night, in which the bulk of the league debuts, is much harder, but if you're dedicated enough, you can catch up on all of the games by the time the Thursday slate begins.By the first Monday of the season, however, the volume starts to overwhelm. There are too many games to see everything. That's why we're here to sort through seven days of NBA action with a batch of winners and losers from the opening week of the 2026-27 season.Who started things off on both the right and wrong foot? Let's dive in.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Philadelphia 76ersThe star-studded starting five looks good, and they spoiled ring nightAs if beating the defending champions on their home floor to spoil ring night wasn't enough, the Philadelphia 76ers proceeded to steal their most famous trick in Game No. 2. When the New York Knicks won their championship against the San Antonio Spurs last June, they did so behind the greatest comeback in playoff history: a 29-point turnaround in Game 4 of the NBA Finals. Well, the 76ers faced New York's Eastern Conference Finals opponent, the Cleveland Cavaliers, in their second game of the season. They came back from a 29-point deficit and won.There are still kinks to work out, especially defensively. There's some stylistic clash here between Joel Embiid's glacial movement and the turbo boosters everyone else on this team seems to play with. But we're already seeing a lot of the ways that the sheer accumulation of talent can manifest into easy points. 
Take this play from the Cleveland comeback. It's a Tyrese Maxey-LeBron James two-man action in which Maxey slips and Sam Merrill shows. That split second gives the fastest player in the NBA a runway to the basket, but watch the help defenders. Donovan Mitchell can't leave Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. Jaylon Tyson offers a half-hearted dig, but he's not going to leave Jaylen Brown. In theory, Evan Mobley should be the one rotating to the basket... except he's guarding Joel Embiid, so by the time he decides to help, Maxey is already gone.
Help defense is a very instinctual trait. Putting this much talent on the floor creates hesitation. Nobody wants to leave an All-Star. What do you do when there are All-Stars everywhere? The Sixers just have so many distinct forms of advantage creation with this star power that they're going to be enormously difficult to defend. Brown is sealing a mismatch in the post? Sorry, can't help, I'm watching Anfernee Simons in the corner. Want to blitz Maxey in a pick-and-roll? Great, now James has a 4-on-3. The Sixers, off to a 3-1 start, torture teams into and out of these difficult, split-second decisions, and it's already paying off big time.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Oklahoma City ThunderOKC had to major injury blows in one nightHas a single championship contender ever lost as much to injury in the first week of a season as the Thunder just did? Jalen Williams is likely out for the year with a dislocated ankle and a fractured fibula. Cason Wallace may be out for the year with a torn labrum. And then, on Monday, Alex Caruso left a win over the Phoenix Suns with a sprained ankle. With Lu Dort gone, the Thunder went from the greatest surplus of All-Defense-caliber wings in NBA history to running out of them practically overnight. Having Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain eases the offensive loss created by Williams' absence, but neither has ever even been a full-time starter. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has never had a greater burden on his shoulders. If he doesn't maintain and perhaps improve upon his MVP-caliber play, Oklahoma City's championship bid is on life support. Chet Holmgren isn't a luxury anymore. He can't disappear against Victor Wembanyama or pick his spots offensively. Those two stars are about to learn what normal NBA depth looks like rather than the embarrassment of riches they've spent their careers with.
        
            
                What Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace injuries mean for the Thunder and why a trade isn't so simple
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Thunder can improve through trade if they want to, but given the typical trade season schedule, reinforcements are months away. Their margin for error is now gone. It's only October, and the Thunder can suddenly no longer afford any further injuries. Oklahoma City looked like the heavy championship favorite when it clobbered San Antonio on opening night. By the end of opening week, the entire championship landscape has shifted.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Minnesota TimberwolvesLaMelo and Ant make up the NBA's most fun team (so far)Chris Finch said before the season that the Timberwolves had "traded moodiness for giddiness" in acquiring LaMelo Ball. Well, no team's attitude adjustment has been more evident early in the season than Minnesota's. No team is loving life quite as much as the Timberwolves to kick off the season. Ball is soft-launching new celebrations. Jaden McDaniels is stomping out imaginary cigarettes. This is the NBA's most fun team through a week.That was the basic idea with the Ball acquisition. The Timberwolves have been a physical, grind-it-out team for the past few seasons, but the entire theory of their team shifted with that trade. This is now a roster built around two of the NBA's best pull-up shooters and the gravity their presence creates. You can no longer double Edwards with impunity because Ball's playmaking destroys mismatches, yet if you don't blitz Edwards off of screens, he's still one of the NBA's most lethal drivers and will simply beat you at the rim. Put all of this together and the Timberwolves have the NBA's sixth-ranked offense through four games while Edwards has already reached 45 points twice.The defense is a work in progress, the shooting outside of Ball and Edwards is hit or miss, and they're turning the ball over a bit too much, but those are rough edges Minnesota can sand down over the course of the season. For now, the revamp is working wonders, and Edwards is playing perhaps the best basketball of his career.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Giannis AntetokounmpoThe Greek Freak's Miami era is not off to the best startGiannis Antetokounmpo prioritized two teams in his trade request from Milwaukee. One made quite a bit of sense: the Boston Celtics, a team with another prime-aged superstar in Jayson Tatum, loads of shooting and a proven regular-season formula. The other was seemingly based more on weather and reputation: the Miami Heat, a Play-In team four years running. Their best player, like Antetokounmpo, was another big man in Bam Adebayo. They had minimal shooting and creation left over, and they had to give up almost everything they had of value to complete the deal without including Adebayo. Naturally, that led to preseason concerns and most of them have thus far manifested as Miami is off to an 0-4 start. There are shooters here and there are defenders here, but there isn't nearly enough overlap between the two. Klay Thompson is getting picked on mercilessly defensively. Tim Hardaway Jr. started the season cold. So have Pelle Larsson and Andrew Wiggins. The notion of building an offense around two big men as your shot creators has thus far proven difficult. What is Antetokounmpo supposed to do when Adebayo works near the rim?
Antetokounmpo himself has been excellent. He's excelling in Miami's fast-paced system and still looks like an MVP candidate, at least offensively. His roster can't say the same. The Heat have a better supporting cast than the Milwaukee Bucks did toward the end, but they're not close to the teams he contended with, nor do they appear all that competitive with the best teams the Eastern Conference has to offer now. Miami has very limited flexibility to improve with, and considering his age and recent history of calf injuries, it's not as though Antetokounmpo should be eager to wait out a multi-year build.
Remember... Antetokounmpo chose this. This is the team he wanted. Maybe he'll be rewarded for that faith as the season progresses. Maybe Pat Riley pulls another shot creator out of his hat. But if this is what the Heat are going to look like, it's worth wondering how worthwhile all of the drama surrounding his exit from Milwaukee really was.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Walker Kessler'Milk Chamberlain' is fitting in perfectly with Luka and the LakersThe official record for dunks in a season is 308, held by Rudy Gobert. Now, let's not get ahead of ourselves, but through three games, Walker Kessler was on pace to dunk 410 times. He's not going to keep dunking five times per game, he's not going to play in all 82 games and he will eventually run into an opponent with some actual size, but Kessler is enjoying one of the biggest teammate-induced glow-ups in recent NBA history.Kessler spent his whole rookie contract playing on a tanking team. His best point guard was probably Mike Conley in his age-35 season. Now he's paired with the greatest lob passer in NBA history in Luka Dončić and another star-level creator in Austin Reaves. No center in the NBA has an easier job offensively than Kessler does right now. We'll be litigating the decision the Lakers made to trade most of their draft capital for Kessler for years. If they don't have enough on the wing to win a title, they have pretty limited means to change that, largely because they have Kessler. But that's a Lakers question. The trade was an undeniable victory for Kessler, who's in the best imaginable circumstances for a player with his skill set.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Stephen CurryIt's already looking like a wasted season for one of the best players of all-timeHere's how Stephen Curry reacted at media day when he was informed that the Golden State Warriors weren't expected to make the playoffs.
Like most of the best jokes, it was funny because it was true. Curry has spent more than a decade genuinely competing at the highest levels of the sport. Merely having him gave the Warriors meaningful championship equity. That window probably closed the moment Jimmy Butler tore his ACL, and Golden State's failure to add LeBron or any meaningful veteran talent this offseason more or less confirmed that. Still, this is Stephen Curry. We at least assumed the final years of his career would end with some dignity.So far, that hasn't been the case. The Lakers mopped the floor with the Warriors on opening night, and then Golden State blew a 12-point lead in the last four minutes against Memphis in their follow-up. The defense ranked 29th entering Monday's game, with Steve Kerr calling out rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who is already picking fits with Dončić, for his performance specifically. Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski are the only Warriors besides Curry offering much of anything offensively.
This probably suits the Warriors themselves just fine. They'll sell out every game because Curry is on the team and they'll probably walk away from this season with the best odds in the newly reformed lottery because having Curry means they'll likely avoid the relegation zone. But everyone else here ensures they don't have a postseason future.It's looking like a sad, wasted season for Curry, who doesn't have too many of them left.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Ty JeromeWho had a Ty Jerome 45-point game on their opening night bingo card?Ty Jerome playing at an All-Star level? Actually, not that surprising. He won't make more runners than anyone else in the league has even attempted as he has thus far... but he's still among the league's best at that particular shot. He won't make more than half of his 3s, but he's a career 39% 3-point shooter, so odds are he'll still make plenty. He had the NBA's eighth-highest offensive Estimated Plus-Minus a year ago, and he ranked 28th on that front in his breakout 2024-25 season for the Cavaliers. On a per-minute basis, Jerome's impact has always been enormous.
But Jerome handling an All-Star's workload? That's new. Entering this season, Jerome had played 30 or more minutes in just 11 regular-season games. He has now done so in all four Grizzlies games this season, and he just played in both halves of a back-to-back on Sunday and Monday. Opening night set a new career-high in field goal attempts. He ranked 15th in the NBA in touches per game before Monday's games.
Durability has always been the concern for Jerome. We're a week into the season, so we can't say whether or not this will last. If it does? His career is about to take off. If Jerome can maintain this workload, he's going to win Most Improved Player running away and probably make an All-Star Team. The Grizzlies wouldn't be playing him this much without real confidence that he could handle it. Case in point: they're still holding Zach Edey to around 22 minutes per game. If Jerome's body has turned some sort of corner that will allow him to keep playing starter minutes, he's about to become one of the most valuable offensive players in basketball.Loser: Orlando MagicAnother year, another notable injury for one of the Magic's starsMake it three consecutive seasons in which Paolo Banchero has suffered a meaningful injury in October or November. In both 2025 and 2026, Franz Wagner suffered injuries around Banchero's return. We can't say for certain that the increased workload overburdens Wagner, but it certainly isn't helping, and the stakes for the Wagner-Banchero partnership this season are higher than ever.
Re-signing key restricted free agent Anthony Black would take the Magic close to the second apron next season, and this is a group that hasn't even won a playoff series yet. They start every season behind the eight ball, and in a conference this deep, that's a recipe for the Play-In Tournament or worse. The Magic are running out of bullets to fire here. They've changed coaches. They've made their all-in trade. If they still can't get over the hump, the Banchero-Wagner questions start to become unavoidable. And to make matters worse, Jalen Suggs, another starter, has a bone bruise.A nice start might have provided some valuable cover as the Magic attempted to answer those questions internally. Now, we're barreling toward another disappointing season and unavoidable, substantial changes to a roster we've never really gotten an extended look at. At least the Jalen Suggs injury wasn't as bad as it looked, but being without him for at least two weeks only makes life harder for the Magic.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Houston RocketsHouston is taking off with Fred VanVleetWhat a difference a point guard makes. Remember how messy Houston's half-court offense looked a year ago without Fred VanVleet? Well, through their first three games, the Rockets scored 106.1 points per 100 plays in the half-court, up from 96.8 a year ago. They scored five more fast-break points per game as well, jumping from 14 to 19 per game. We haven't seen much Steven Adams yet, but it's worth noting, as per usual, that the Rockets had a 40% offensive rebound rate in his lone, nine-minute appearance thus far this season.The Rockets traded for Kevin Durant in the summer of 2025, expecting to have one sort of team. Losing VanVleet and, later, Adams turned them into a different, inferior team. This season is their shot at a mulligan, and three early wins to kick things off suggest that they're going to make the most of it.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: New Orleans PelicansMore head-scratching from one of the NBA's most confusing teamsIt's time for the Bayou's favorite annual tradition: the Pelicans wasting a good player. Last year, they DNP-CD'd Jose Alvarado on opening night. They wound up trading him for loose change and he proceeded to become an essential part of an NBA champion. This year, they thought they'd raise the stakes with a higher-profile player.What on Earth is happening with Herbert Jones? Why is the best and perhaps only defender on this team playing 17 minutes a game? He comes with obvious offensive deficiencies, of course, but they're still starting two non-shooting big men and are at the bottom of the league in 3-point attempt rate anyway, so they might as well get a defensive bump out of their questionable shot profile. He was the 10th-most used Pelicans player in Saturday's disastrous collapse against the Denver Nuggets, one in which Jamal Murray torched them for 42 points. Jones was his primary defender on just a single shot attempt, according to NBA.com tracking data. He played less than Jordan Poole.If this is how the Pelicans felt about Jones or his fit on the roster, why didn't they trade him over the summer? There would have been suitors. The longer this goes on, the lower his trade value slips. We're now entering the second season under this Joe Dumars regime, and what exactly his long-term vision here is remains a mystery.

title: Kawhi Leonard sidelined with knee injury, which means he'll miss his return to Clippers' Intuit Dome - CBS Sports
description: Leonard will not be on the floor as the Raptors make their only trip to L.A. next week

        Kawhi Leonard will miss at least one week with swelling in his left knee. The Toronto Raptors said on Tuesday that the star will go through a treatment and rehabilitation plan for his knee and be reevaluated in a week. The positive note in the release is that an MRI "revealed no acute injury" but given Leonard's injury history, him missing time this early in the season with knee discomfort and swelling is a concern for a Raptors team that had hopes of contending in a stout Eastern Conference. Leonard played in the first two wins of the season for Toronto against the Bulls and the Wizards, averaging 19.5 points and 7.5 rebounds in those two starts but was off with his shooting to start the year. Then on Sunday he sat out with knee discomfort in a loss to the Timberwolves, and now he will miss at least a week of action and potentially more. 
With a timetable of one week from Tuesday for his reevaluation, Leonard will miss at least the next four games for the Raptors. That includes Toronto's lone trip to Los Angeles this season, where they'll play a back-to-back against the Lakers on Sunday and the Clippers on Monday. So this injury means Leonard will not be playing at the Intuit Dome this season.Leonard was traded to the Raptors from the Clippers this summer. The deal did not officially go through until the league finished its investigation into the Clippers and salary cap circumvention involving Leonard. The Clippers were severely punished by the NBA (losing five first-round picks, getting hit with a $30 million fine and seeing owner Steve Ballmer and other executives suspended), while Leonard got traded and only had to pay a $700,000 fine. 
Leonard's return to the Intuit Dome figured to be greeted with plenty of animosity from the Clippers faithful for how his tenure there ended. But fans will have to keep waiting to greet Leonard back.

title: Deion Sanders allegedly offered critics $50K to stop talking about him - CBS Sports

body:
Sanders was once college football's most polarizing figure, and allegedly offered critics big money to keep his name out of their mouths

        Deion Sanders' Colorado Buffaloes sit at the bottom of the Big 12 amid an active five-game losing streak that's dropped them to 2-5 overall and 0-3 in conference play. Over the past two seasons, the Buffaloes have gone 1-11 in the Big 12, and all of the excitement of Sanders' first two seasons in Boulder has turned to either frustration or apathy. Early in his tenure, Sanders was a lightning rod in the world of college sports, drawing more attention than just about anyone else. Whether it was praise or criticism, Sanders was one of the sport's top draws, and while Sanders publicly embraced his role as college football's most polarizing figure, he also regularly challenged his critics. Apparently, that included offering them money to stop talking about him, with his videographer, Uncle Neely, claiming Sanders offered some critics $50,000 not to talk about him for a year."For the most part, the people that attack him wouldn't be making the money they were making if he wasn't here to attack," Neely said on BuffBoys Live. "Which is why he told some of them, 'Hey man, let's just do this. I give you $50,000 to not mention my name for a year.' And ain't nobody took the deal yet. . . . And you love talking about this man so much, and you make so much talking of this man that you turned the deal down."
The Buffaloes, as a program, aren't in a position to afford to move on from Sanders, who would be owed $25.5 million in buyout money if he were fired after the end of the 2026 season. Sanders has spent the last two years insisting his team is close and that they're doing all the right things, but it's just not showing up on Saturdays. "We're so disciplined in this and that, and this and that, and every darn thing we do, but it seems like as soon as we go in the field, we're not disciplined," Sanders said after Saturday's loss to Oklahoma State. "I really don't understand it, because we are disciplined in every area of this program. When it comes to academics, when it comes to being somewhere on time, when it comes to wearing the proper uniform, when it comes to just your manners in the building. Everything. But [when] we get on the field at the most critical moments, we blow it."The more Sanders leans on that refrain, the harder it becomes for the fans to buy it. The result is growing apathy around the Colorado program, as there isn't a clear path out of the Big 12's basement, and they have to hope Sanders can be the coach to pull them out. 
That stands in stark contrast to the vibe in Boulder a few years ago, when there was so much chatter about Sanders that his top critics would allegedly turn down $50,000 not to speak about him for a year.

title: Angel Reese, Karl Smesko blast officiating after Dream fall into 3-2 WNBA Finals hole to Valkyries - CBS Sports
description: 'The contact they allow on Angel compared to everybody else is just ridiculous,' Smesko said
body:
'The contact they allow on Angel compared to everybody else is just ridiculous,' Smesko said

        A few days ago, the Atlanta Dream were up 2-1 in the 2026 WNBA Finals with a chance to take a commanding 3-1 lead at home. Now, after a 64-55 loss in Game 5 on Monday, they suddenly find themselves down 3-2 and on the brink of elimination. Following one of the worst offensive performances in Finals history, Angel Reese and coach Karl Smesko took their frustration out on the officials.  "I'm still trying to figure out how to play through the physicality. I mean, a lot of us are getting fouled and they're not calling it, or we're talking to the ref after and they're saying, 'Oh, we'll get you next time.' So it is a little frustrating in the moment of it," Reese said. "I'm kinda used to it, because this was happening throughout the season, so I just have to continue to play through it." Reese was dominant in Games 2 and 3, as she became the third player ever with a 30-point, 15-rebound game in the Finals, and joined A'ja Wilson as the only players with back-to-back 20-point, 10-rebound games in the Finals. But in the last two games, she's gotten nothing going offensively.  Reese scored eight points on 2 of 12 shooting in Game 4, and seven points on 2 of 8 in Game 5. This was the first time in Reese's career that she's made two or fewer shots in consecutive games, and the first time she's been held in single digits in consecutive games since early in her rookie season.  
In addition to the missed shots, Reese has not been able to get to the free throw line lately. She averaged 7.6 free throw attempts in the first three games of the series, but has only taken 10 total in the last two games. Her four free throw attempts in Game 5 were her fewest of the postseason.   Reese said that she "definitely" noticed an uptick in the physicality from the Valkyries starting in Game 4.  "There was also a possession [in Game 4] where Gabby [Williams] pulled me on purpose, and she was screaming, 'Foul, foul, foul,' and they didn't call it. So that defintely was frustrating for sure. Her team is saying it, and they're all screaming 'foul,' but the refs, I don't know what's going on, why they can't hear it?" Reese said.  
"When I do switch on the post, and I'm a lot stronger than the opponent, I should be able to turn, and they're calling an offensive foul, but I'm getting pushed before that, so that is frustrating for sure," she continued. "It definitely shifted when we went up 2-1. Things shifted and I don't know what happened, but it definitely took a big turn." Points have been hard to come by all series for both teams, but the Dream's offense was particularly poor in Game 5. They shot 29.2% from the field, which was the fourth-worst team field goal percentage in a Finals game in WNBA history, and scored 55 points, which was tied for the 10th-fewest points ever in a Finals game. And this time, they weren't able to get to the line to supplement the poor shotmaking.  Dream's free throw attempts in the FinalsGameFTFTAFT%1 				18 				21 				85.7% 				2 				30 				35 				85.7% 				3 				20 				29 				69% 				4 				22 				31 				71% 				5 				11 				14 				78.6% 				"I give them credit for playing good defense. They're known for their defense and they've been playing great defense throughout the series, but I do want to have Angel's back here," Smesko said. "The contact they allow on Angel compared to everybody else is just ridiculous. Just ridiculous. We should have gone to the foul line six-to-eight more times just on that."In Games 2-4, the Dream became just the second team to attempt at least 25 free throws in three straight Finals games, per ESPN. And for the series, they still have a significant edge at the line, where they've outscored the Valkyries by 42 points. TeamFTFTAFT%Dream10113077.7%Valkyries597875.6%Even so, Smesko has not liked what he's seen from the officials in the last few games. "To miss double-dribbles and travels, multiple that always led to points, you can't be at this level and make this many mistakes," Smesko said. "There's things that are on us. We're missing shots we should make. But at the same time, that needs to be a whole lot better than it was. It's time that if you push somebody with two hands as they drive, it's gotta be a foul. I'm kinda tired of some of the excuses that I'm hearing."

title: Who's the World Series MVP frontrunner? Plus more pressing questions for Brewers vs. Rays Game 4 - CBS Sports
description: The Brewers are going for a sweep and their first World Series championship on Tuesday night
body:
The Brewers are going for a sweep and their first World Series championship on Tuesday night

    11:54 am ET

            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After a 10-1 ritual dismantling by the Milwaukee Brewers on Monday night, the Tampa Bay Rays are down 3-0 in the best-of-seven World Series and face an elimination game in Tuesday night's Game 4 (8 p.m. ET).The odds of a comeback in the series are all but insurmountable. Across all of Major League Baseball postseason history up until now, 42 teams have been down 3-0, and only one – the 2004 Boston Red Sox – has come back to win the series in question. Stated another way, history suggests the Rays have a mere 2.4% chance of pulling off the miracle comeback and winning four straight from the Brewers. Really, though, it may be even harder than that. Teams down 0-3 who began the series on the road, as the Rays did, have been down 0-3 18 times in MLB postseason history and lost all of those series. There is slightly more hope when it comes to extending the series. Teams down 0-3 in MLB postseason series have won Game 4 23.8% of the time. That really has to be the focus for Kevin Cash and the on-the-brink Rays – to survive another day. Speaking of which, that brings us to three questions for Game 4 – the answers to which will determine whether the Rays can survive long enough to force a Game 5 and maybe just maybe begin chiseling out a baseball miracle. Let's get to it. 
Will the Rays finally break through against the Milwaukee bullpen?One of the biggest on-paper edges for the Brewers coming into this series was the depth of Pat Murphy's bullpen. Indeed, the Brewers bullpen has been all but impregnable in this World Series and indeed throughout the entire postseason. This is best exemplified by lefty relief ace Aaron Ashby, who this postseason has to allow a run in eight appearances. Across those eight appearances, he's worked 15 ⅔ innings and allowed just five hits with 17 strikeouts and three walks. Not surprisingly, those have been high-leverage innings, to boot. Overall, the Milwaukee bullpen has authored the following numbers: SpanInningsERAK%2026 Playoffs53 ⅔1.3425.5%2026 World Series131.3828.6%By comparison, the Rays' bullpen during this World Series has a 6.17 ERA and a K% of 8.3. That, more than anything, has been the differentiator thus far. Game 4 figures to be a bullpen-heavy game for Murphy and Milwaukee and perhaps a full-on bullpen game. Brandon Woodruff had been slated to be the Game 4 opener, but his appearance in the Game 3 blowout probably changes those plans. Whatever the specifics, Tampa Bay is going to have to find its way to doing some damage against the deep and excellent Brewers pen if it's going to survive another day. Along similar lines, the Rays badly need to get some length out of starter Griffin Jax in Game 4 so as to minimize their reliance on the bullpen. Jax, though, hasn't lasted more than four innings in a start in more than a month. Will Junior Caminero's power show up?
This World Series so far has not been rich with power, as the two teams have combined for just two home runs through the first three games. Heck, the Brewers in their 10-run onslaught in Game 3 didn't even hit a ball to the pull field. During the regular season, neither of these teams was especially reliant on home run power, but the Rays scored a higher percentage of their runs via the longball than the Brewers did. In other words, this present power outage has been more damaging to Tampa Bay. Writ small, we have Junior Caminero, the Rays' 23-year-old rising star and their richest power source. During the regular season, he smacked 42 home runs and averaged a homer every 14.7 at-bats. During these playoffs, however, he's got only one home run in 43 at-bats. That lone home run came in the American League Championship Series against Cleveland. Nothing would help the Tampa Bay cause of forcing a Game 5 like a Caminero uprising on Tuesday night. It's overdue, for sure. Who will be the World Series MVP?The Brewers need to win one game before the Rays win four in order to hoist the World Series trophy for the first time in franchise history. As such, the 2026 World Series MVP is overwhelmingly likely to be a Brewer. That leads us to the following question: William Contreras or Jackson Chourio?Each has a strong case for the honor. Most Valuable Brewer?Jackson Chourio and William Contreras both have outstanding numbers in this World Series.ChourioContreras.571AVG.538.571OBP.571.643SLG.5382RBI34R1Contreras, the Brewers' catcher and warrior-poet, has snuffed out the usually potent Tampa Bay running game, handled the pitching staff with his usual aplomb, shown a knack and timely and successful ABS challenges, and more than done his job at the plate. Through the first three games of this series, Contreras has put up a slash line of .538/.571/.538 with a walk, three RBI, and a run scored. As for the 22-year-old Chourio, he's fresh off a four-hit performance in Game 3, and for the series, he's batting .571/.571/.643 with three steals in as many attempts, and four runs scored. It's hard to overlook Contreras' broad-based excellence this series, but Chourio may have the momentum. Sal Frelick and Ashby could certainly state their cases with a standout performance and Game 4, but right now it looks like Contreras or Chourio.

title: How the Rays were broken by the merciless Brewers, who are on the verge of a World Series sweep - CBS Sports
description: The Rays' chances at a comeback appeared to fall apart when the Brewers scored eight two-out runs in the fifth in
body:
The Rays' chances at a comeback appeared to fall apart when the Brewers scored eight two-out runs in the fifth inning of Game 3
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:52 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — There comes a time in every battle when exhaustion overtakes reason. When the body can no longer summon what the spirit demands. When even hope, sometimes, the most stubborn of human instincts, begins to surrender.Then comes the cruelest realization of all. The one that settles in the pit of one's stomach before creeping between the ears and whispering:We can't beat these guys.For the Rays, that realization might have arrived in the top of the fifth inning of Monday's Game 3 beatdown at the hands of the Brewers.Their hearts were ripped from their chests beneath the gaze of a sold-out Tropicana Field, where 40,388 fans gathered, hoping to witness redemption. Instead, they were left with a reckoning.
A 10-1 reckoning, to be exact, one that puts them on the brink of elimination of this year's World Series.It's easy to point to the seven straight hits that produced eight runs. All with two outs. But look a little closer. The resignation began long before the pain set in. Before the pulse came to a bludgeoned halt.The tone was set when Jackson Chourio laced his third straight single off Freddy Peralta with one out in the fifth.
That's when the bullpen began to stir.That's when Peralta's pitch count continued its climb toward 87 on the evening. That's when his breaths grew deeper, as though he sensed the bloodbath awaiting him if he couldn't regain command. That's when his mechanics began to betray him, landing too soon on his front side and robbing him of his usual extension.And that's when he began reaching for the bill of his cap a little more frequently, searching for something to occupy his hands while his mind wrestled with the inevitable: The Brewers."I think they're good at not trying to do too much," Peralta said afterward. "They do a good job of putting the ball in play know, trying to pull the ball in play and taking a walk. I think I was feeling good but my changeup wasn't landing well tonight."
He got Jake Bauers to fly out. But then Chourio stole second. And then he walked Christian Yelich on six pitches.Cameron Booser got the call out of the Rays bullpen after that. As did Cole Sulser.Reality had finally washed ashore. The very reality the Rays had spent the evening trying to outrun, only to lose themselves in the effort.
Seven straight hits. Eight runs. All with two outs. A 2-0 lead had suddenly become a 10-run burial ground."They were spitting on good pitches and putting balls in play," said Booser, who yielded four runs in that inning without recording an out. It's a good lineup. Things seem to be going their way right now, so it's unfortunate. Worst feeling in the world. You feel like you're let your team down." But this is what the Brewers do.They unraveled and mocked a Dodgers juggernaut that looked capable of rivaling the Yankees dynasties of the late 1990s and early 2000s.
They dare their opponents to take a lead, just so they can snatch it back.They dare opposing lineups to go scoreless through the first four or five innings, knowing what awaits once the game falls into the hands of men named Uribe, Ashby, Megill, Romero and Hall.Imagine that dread creeping in.Opposing hitters grip their bats a little tighter.Defenders begin moving a little faster than the game demands.Just look at Tampa Bay, one of baseball's most fundamentally sound clubs, now withering beneath the pressure Milwaukee has become so adept at manufacturing.Victor Mesa Jr.'s third-inning miscue cost the Rays a run. It was the club's third error in two games.
The Brewers don't merely capitalize on mistakes. They make opponents fear committing them."With them, they are executing really well, and that's what the results say," Tampa outfielder Chandler Simpson said.But the execution is only just a sliver of the torment. Because what does it really mean for William Contreras to challenge a pitch called a ball to Junior Caminero, and once again be right, in the bottom of the fifth inning, other than to administer another dose of novocaine to the Rays' already numbing pain?
Or for Sal Frelick to lay out for a diving grab in the eighth inning with a 10-run lead, other than to preserve what was then a staff-wide one-hitter?This is what got them here.The Brewers want to bury their opposition. Yield no mercy. Leave no memory of what success might feel like, just in case their opponents start believing in it again.Or, as their manager, Pat Murphy, puts it: "We want to step on your throat."And they have. In the harshest of fashions.Milwaukee allowed Tampa Bay to believe it could compete through the first two contests, winning each by a single run, only to strong-arm the Rays like a father who's grown tired of letting his child believe he can win an innocent roughhousing match.
The Brewers took down Nick Martinez, Drew Rasmussen and Peralta just as they had dispatched Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Blake Snell.Griffin Jax awaits. Just as Tyler Glasnow did in the NLCS two weeks ago.The Rays can't beat these guys. Not this group. And inside the clubhouse, much like Los Angeles after Game 3, there was a sense of that. There's still more to play. The Rays know that. They will compete. But still, there was a sense of peace, not demoralization, hanging over the Tampa Bay clubhouse. The Rays haven't played their best baseball. But sometimes, the explanation is simpler than anyone wants to admit.
The other team is just better. The Brewers are just better. And now they stand one victory away from the first World Series championship in franchise history."This is a best-of-seven series," said Murphy. "It looks like we're in the driver's seat, but it's baseball. Anything can happen. I like the way we battle. I'm going to choose us when we can." At this point, the Rays might choose Milwaukee, too.

title: Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe apologizes after Mao meme comments amid growing backlash in China - CBS Sports
description: The French striker was widely criticised in China after his comments on a meme involving him and Mao Zedong
body:
The French striker was widely criticised in China after his comments on a meme involving him and Mao Zedong
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:38 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe issued an apology Tuesday after comments he made about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong led several sponsors to drop him and drew a backlash from Chinese state television. The day after the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony, which saw Mbappe leave the London Palladium empty-handed, began with an international drama involving China, Mbappe and LaLiga. It all started when Mbappe told French talk show "The Bridge" that the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator..." The clip also showed Mbappe's face on an image resembling Mao.  To put that into context, a recurring joke, repeated in multiple memes, associates Mbappe with the word "dictator" for his influence in the sport and for how he interacts with teammates and players. During the 2026 World Cup, 2025 Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembele called him "Mbappe Mobut," referring to Mobutu, the dictator who ran the Democratic Republic of Congo for more than 30 years. In September, Mbappe addressed the memes in an interview with France Football, saying that while he understood the jokes, they "sometimes reveal a lack of political and human awareness among people. There's a side that's a bit less funny, because we know the damage people like that have caused throughout history. Being compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions upon millions of people miserable... I don't think I've done that in my life."  Two Chinese brands that have deals with the French striker issued statements condemning the player's statements. Mengniu, the country's largest dairy producer, wrote that it, "firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people." Later on Tuesday, drinks giant Dongpeng issued a statement as well. "Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments." According to the state-owned Global Times newspaper, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV's apps won't feature news related to the player, and the broadcaster will also stop streaming LaLiga matches.Why is it a big topic?Mao is obviously one of the most famous figures in modern China's history. He founded the People's Republic of China in 1949 and led the Communist Party until his death in 1976. Much has changed in China since his death, but the Chinese Communist Party still governs the country and sees jokes and memes about Mao as an insult to the party and the nation. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said, "We have noted the relevant reports. Words and deeds that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with opposition from all sectors of Chinese society."How Mbappe and LaLiga respondedThe French striker issued a statement about the matter: "During a recent interview with me, I commented on an image of myself, but my comment was not appropriate, and I now realise that it hurt the feelings of many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone whom my words upset, as that was never my intention at all. I hold deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I express my sincere regret." 
LaLiga also issued a statement, defending the agreement they still have in place with Chinese state television. "LALIGA deeply regrets the offence caused to Chinese fans by Kylian Mbappé's recent comments. These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent LALIGA. Within the scope of our institutional responsibility, we apologise on behalf of LALIGA and all its clubs. Spanish football stands for respect, coexistence and unity among people from all cultures. We extend our respect to China, its institutions and its people, and deeply value the support of the millions of fans who follow us every week. We reaffirm our commitment to a relationship built over many years. We are working with our partners and institutional counterparts in China to address this situation. Furthermore, in collaboration with clubs and players, we will introduce an awareness and communication protocol aimed at promoting respect for different cultures and helping to prevent similar situations in the future." 
LaLiga president Javier Tebas, who recently also had multiple public disagreements with Real Madrid, wrote on X he "cannot allow the actions of an individual to tarnish this relationship or harm the more than 20 clubs competing in our professional leagues and the millions of Chinese fans. We are taking all measures within our power and working directly with our partners and counterparts in China to resolve this situation."

        Auburn basketball fired general manager Brian Kloman Monday, just nine days before the Tigers' season-opening tilt against Southeastern Louisiana and just seven months after hiring him away from Louisville. The dismissal stems from an eligibility issue surrounding Lithuanian wing Mantas Rubstavicius, who was not cleared by the NCAA and was attempting to earn a temporary restraining order to gain eligibility.Kloman served as the point-man on the Rubstavicius recruitment. Kloman hid that Rubstavicius had once been enrolled in university courses in Europe, which changed the calculus for his eligibility case, per Auburn247's Nathan King. Rubstavicius' representation originally believed the 24-year-old had a case to play college basketball because he was within his five-year window of graduating from high school and was attempting to begin his collegiate education at Auburn. But enrolling in university courses in Europe is a major hurdle for NCAA eligibility because it starts the five-year eligibility window. Rubstavicius, apparently, was not a first-time student. That key detail was hidden by Kloman and wrecked Rubstavicius' case to play college hoops.

Rubstavicius was slated to be a real piece for second-year coach Steven Pearl after Auburn jumped through numerous hoops to land his commitment, including paying a €300,000 buyout to Žalgiris Kaunas, the top-shelf Lithuanian club. Expectations aren't sky-high for Auburn in Year 2 under Pearl --- the Tigers were picked 10th in CBS Sports' SEC preview. title: Jerry Jones on a possible role for Troy Aikman with the Cowboys: 'Don't rule it out' - CBS Sports
description: Aikman won three Super Bowls with the Cowboys in the 1990s

Aikman won three Super Bowls with the Cowboys in the 1990s

        Jerry Jones is the owner and general manager of the Dallas Cowboys. That much is not going to change, no matter what. We know that not only from years of watching him operate, but also from his direct quotes over the nearly 40 years that he's owned the team. But that doesn't mean there can't or won't be changes and/or additions to the Cowboys' front office. And apparently, we shouldn't close the door on something like that happening with a prominent former Cowboys quarterback: Troy Aikman.Jones was asked during a Monday morning radio appearance on 105.3 The Fan about the possibility of Aikman joining the Cowboys in a major role, and he didn't rule it out."The answer is not that necessarily we're going to do something more direct with the team at this time, but don't rule it out," Jones said, via The Athletic. "It's very possible."
Aikman is currently employed as the lead analyst on ESPN's "Monday Night Football" broadcast, and has spent the last 26 years calling games for either ESPN or FOX. But he was also recently hired as a consultant for the Miami Dolphins, whom he helped during their search for a new general manager, which ultimately resulted in their hiring former Packers executive Jon-Eric Sullivan.Of course, Aikman is better known for having won three Super Bowls with the Cowboys in the 1990s, so he has extensive ties to the organization. However, he's also been openly critical of the team — up to and including Jerry Jones himself — in the past."I think that teams and organizations, whether it's sports, business, I think it all does start at the top, good or bad," Aikman said this offseason when discussing the Cowboys' Super Bowl drought. "I think it starts at the top. I don't think Jerry would shy away from that. I think Jerry would certainly take responsibility. He'll take accountability if and when they win, and I think then you have to take responsibility when it hasn't worked out. And it hasn't worked out."
It's interesting that Jones would still consider potentially bringing Aikman into the organization in the wake of those and other comments that he's made over the years in his capacity as a broadcaster and analyst. But ultimately, Jones will do whatever it takes to bring attention to the Cowboys, and hiring Aikman in some capacity would certainly do that. Whether it would result in their actually getting back to and winning the Super Bowl is, obviously, another story.This year's Cowboys team fancied itself a Super Bowl contender coming into the season, for example, but has instead been up and down at best. The Cowboys did snap their two-game losing skid with a win over the Eagles on Monday night, but Aikman himself remained unconvinced that their latest win was a sign that they're contenders again."Eh, not really. Not really. And I don't mean that as a negative," Aikman said when asked that very question during an appearance on the postgame edition of SportsCenter with Scott Van Pelt. "This is a beat-up Philadelphia team. To come in here and win tonight, I mean, let's not get carried away. They kind of did what you would expect them to do."
Dallas is just 3-4 after the victory, sitting behind the New York Giants in the NFC East standings. The Cowboys do have a somewhat favorable schedule coming up, with games against the Arizona Cardinals, Indianapolis Colts, Tennessee Titans and the Eagles again over the next five weeks, but we've seen them stumble even with a favorable schedule before. (They also have a game against the San Francisco 49ers during that stretch.) We likely won't get a better idea of their contender status until the stretch surrounding their bye week, when they play the Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams, Jacksonville Jaguars and Giants in succession. If yet another year goes by where they don't accomplish what Jones wants to accomplish, perhaps a significant change like hiring Aikman for a front-office or consultant role is something that comes to fruition next offseason.

title: Kamario Taylor out for season: Mississippi State star QB requires surgery on injured toe - CBS Sports
description: The Bulldogs' QB was one of the breakout stars early in 2026, but he will now miss the rest of the season
body:
The Bulldogs' QB was one of the breakout stars early in 2026, but he will now miss the rest of the season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:25 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Mississippi State star quarterback Kamario Taylor will miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to his toe injury that will likely require surgery, sources confirmed to CBS Sports' John Talty. Taylor was one of the breakout stars early in the year with monster performances in wins against Minnesota, South Carolina and Missouri that put Mississippi State inside the top 25. In that win over Missouri, Taylor suffered a turf toe injury that he tried to play through against Alabama before sitting out Mississippi State's loss to LSU. After seeing his Bulldogs get shut out by the Tigers, Taylor attempted to come back against Oklahoma last week but exited in the first half after pulling up on a fourth-down scramble and leaving for the locker room. What losing Taylor for the season means for the BulldogsWithout Taylor, Mississippi State's offense has struggled mightily, and at 4-3 with four games left against SEC foes, the Bulldogs are far from guaranteed a bowl trip with their star quarterback now done for the year. 
After getting blanked by LSU, the Bulldogs managed 15 points (all in the second half after Taylor went out) in a loss to Oklahoma. Parker Puckett steps into the starting quarterback role now for the Bulldogs and has big shoes to fill with how much Taylor was doing to make Mississippi State a dynamic offense. The good news for Mississippi State and Puckett is that star running back Fluff Bothwell is back this week after missing the Oklahoma game with an injury of his own. Bothwell leads the team with 91 carries for 514 yards and three touchdowns on the ground, and figures to be a focal point of Mississippi State's offensive game plan moving forward to take some of the pressure off of Puckett. The Bulldogs are on the road at No. 11 Texas this week before a stretch of three consecutive home games that will be their best chance to get bowl-eligible. Mississippi State will welcome Vanderbilt, Auburn and Tennessee Tech to Starkville before a trip north to Oxford for the Egg Bowl on Black Friday. 
Scrapping just to get to a bowl wasn't what Bulldogs fans envisioned while watching Taylor carve up defenses the first four games of the season, but unfortunately that's now the reality in Starkville with their star done for the year. What does Taylor's future look likeAs for Taylor, the focus shifts to 2027, when he could become one of college football's top stars. He will have Heisman and NFL Draft buzz heading into his junior season, and will focus on getting healthy and getting his body right to play a full season in a pivotal year for his future. Taylor's dynamic passing ability pops off the screen when watching him. Even with the missed time the last two weeks, he still leads the SEC in touchdown passes with 17, and with prototypical size and a cannon for an arm, scouts can't help but drool over his potential. If he can put a full season on film next year, he will be one of the top prospects for the 2028 NFL Draft, but doing so will require another step forward because teams will be game planning for him in a way they might not have early this season. 
If that's to happen in Starkville, Mississippi State will have to fend off the vultures when it comes to keeping Taylor in town as quarterback-needy programs will undoubtedly lob massive offers at Taylor to pry him out of Mississippi. However, Taylor has been vocal about his desire to remain a Bulldog and provided Mississippi State can put together a competitive offer -- which shouldn't be a hard sell to boosters after what he did to start this season -- they'll have a great chance to keep the Macon, Mississippi native in maroon and white. If that's the case, the Bulldogs will also need to invest in the pieces around him. Keeping Bothwell as his backfield mate would be one step, and bolstering his wide receiving corps and offensive line to protect him will be priorities for Jeff Lebby and the Bulldogs' personnel staff this coming offseason. Mississippi State knows how important it is to maximize a year where you have an elite talent at quarterback -- the Dak Prescott era was the high point of Bulldogs football this century. Taylor can be that kind of program-changing talent, and now it's incumbent on Mississippi State to go all-in as best they can to capitalize in 2027.

title: SEC Power Rankings, Week 9: Texas gets redemption as the mayhem only intensifies - CBS Sports
description: What exactly am I supposed to make of the SEC this season? No, seriously, I need some help.This league cannibalizes itself on a weekly b
body:
What exactly am I supposed to make of the SEC this season? No, seriously, I need some help.This league cannibalizes itself on a weekly basis, which essentially twists my brain into a pretzel as I attempt to organize these rankings. Texas is one of the biggest conundrums.Two weeks ago, the Longhorns looked helpless against a sophomore quarterback making his first career start in their loss to Florida. Fast forward one week, and Texas neutralized the best quarterback in the conference as it forced Trinidad Chambliss into three interceptions en route to a massive win over Ole Miss.Then there's the transitive property. Tennessee suffered a heartbreaking road loss to South Carolina, which got boat-raced by Alabama -- the same Alabama team that the Volunteers pushed around at Neyland Stadium.
The only thing you can count on in the SEC this year is that no team can be counted on from one week to another. That makes for a ton of excitement as a fan, but it makes for a headache when putting together power rankings, though I bravely accepted that task again this week.As the conference eats itself alive, here are the updated SEC Power Rankings.
        
            
                CBS Sports 138: UCLA soars into top five, Miami sits as unanimous No. 1 in college football rankings
                
                    Chip Patterson                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Georgia BulldogsLast week: 1Because the SEC is a mess, Georgia remained atop the rankings through a loss and an open date. The Bulldogs will have a chance to earn their spot this weekend in a rivalry game against Florida in Atlanta. Georgia is riding a five-game winning streak in that series, but the Gators entered their open date coming off a huge win over Texas. It'll be interesting to see how Kirby Smart and his team respond after a stunning loss to Auburn.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Kentucky WildcatsLast week: 3Another week, another win for Kentucky. The Wildcats overcame a slow start against Vanderbilt and are guaranteed to begin November at 7-1, right in the thick of the College Football Playoff race. Quarterback Kenny Minchey has been a great fit in Will Stein's offense, completing 69% of his passes for 1,755 yards, 14 touchdowns and just one interception. It's been a while since Kentucky was this strong at the quarterback position.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. LSU TigersLast week: 4Are the Tigers starting to hit their stride as we roll toward the home stretch? Since losing to Kentucky, LSU has crushed Mississippi State and Auburn by a combined score of 69-17. There is some context needed there because the Bulldogs didn't have Kamario Taylor, but Lane Kiffin's offense has been dominant. Sam Leavitt may finally be getting healthy, and the return of star tight end Trey'Dez Green is huge. The Tigers might prefer to play again on Saturday to keep this momentum before hosting Alabama, but they'll get a week off instead.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Texas LonghornsLast week: 8Figuring out which Texas team will show up from one week to the next -- or one play to the next -- is an impossible task. The Longhorns were everything from national championship contender to SEC also-ran against Ole Miss, but the good outweighed the bad in a critical win. Despite a couple of mistakes, Arch Manning answered the call and did enough to keep the critics at bay, and the defense held up extremely well against Trinidad Chambliss. That game was proof that Texas can be a juggernaut when everything comes together, but how long will it be until Mr. Hyde shows up again?
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Alabama Crimson TideLast week: 6Things got a little sweaty in Tuscaloosa when Texas A&M took a three-point lead in the second half, but Keelon Russell put on his cape and delivered a relatively stress-free win for Alabama in the fourth quarter. The Crimson Tide still can't run the ball effectively, but that doesn't matter when Russell and the receivers are firing on all cylinders. Can Kalen DeBoer bank on that against LSU in Baton Rouge coming out of the open date? The Tide have to unlock something on the ground over the next two weeks because they can't be one-dimensional in Death Valley.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Ole Miss RebelsLast week: 2Ole Miss showed some serious resolve by digging out of a 21-point hole in Austin, but it couldn't complete the comeback. A horrific first half was ultimately too much to overcome, and Trinidad Chambliss played his worst game of the season. A run defense that improved coming out of the open date regressed, allowing 207 yards to the Longhorns. The Rebels' playoff fate may come down to the Georgia matchup on Nov. 7, but it has to get past a wounded Auburn team first.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Tennessee VolunteersLast week: 5The Volunteers blew a terrific opportunity to enter November with one College Football Playoff mulligan available. Twelve total penalties -- three of which wiped out touchdowns -- and a botched fourth-and-1 attempt resulted in a soul-crushing loss. Tennessee now has two weeks to sit with that disappointment before a top-10 Kentucky team rolls into Neyland Stadium. With zero margin for error left, Tennessee can't afford to keep shooting itself in the foot.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Florida GatorsLast week: 9With the Gators coming out of the open date, all eyes are on the quarterback position against Georgia. Sophomore Tramell Jones led Florida to a road win over Texas with Aaron Philo injured, but did Jones play well enough to lock down the job? He wasn't very efficient through the air but extended plays and picked up extra yardage with his legs. Jon Sumrall isn't giving anything away, and there could be a slight edge in forcing Kirby Smart to prepare for both quarterbacks.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. South Carolina GamecocksLast week: 12Cocktober believers were validated on Saturday night as fans rushed the field at Williams-Brice Stadium. Is South Carolina poised for another midseason turnaround, similar to the 2024 season? The Gamecocks have a very favorable schedule down the stretch, and if LaNorris Sellers plays the way he did against Tennessee, that offense will be a handful. That unit will be tested again this weekend as South Carolina travels to Norman to clash with Oklahoma, though it may not take many points to come away with a win.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Missouri TigersLast week: 9The return of Ahmad Hardy is excellent news for everyone involved. If Hardy can get back into game shape for the home stretch, the Tigers will have the best backfield in the country. Jamal Roberts already ranks seventh nationally with 867 yards, and Hardy finished second last season with 1,649 rushing yards. Missouri probably won't need reinforcements against Arkansas this weekend, but Hardy could be a huge boost when the team faces Texas and Georgia in the coming weeks.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    11. Oklahoma SoonersLast week: 13I don't want to give the Sooners too much credit for beating Mississippi State without Kamario Taylor for most of the game, but the offense put up a rare respectable performance against a Power Four opponent. That's something! John Mateer totaled 320 yards and two passing touchdowns (with zero turnovers), and Isaiah Sategna III torched the Bulldogs for 164 receiving yards and a score. Maybe that gives Oklahoma some confidence going into the South Carolina game.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    12. Auburn TigersLast week: 10The high of a win over No. 1 Georgia was followed by a demolition at the hands of LSU. The Tigers were never really competitive in that game, and the offensive line was an unmitigated disaster. Auburn averaged just 1.9 yards per attempt on the ground, and it allowed seven sacks and 12 tackles for loss. Life for the Tigers may get worse before it gets better because they have to play what I can only assume is a frustrated Ole Miss team in Oxford.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    13. Mississippi State BulldogsLast week: 11With Kamario Taylor battling injury, Mississippi State hasn't been able to muster any kind of threat offensively. The Bulldogs have now lost three games in a row, and it may be time to give Appalachian State transfer AJ Swann a look at quarterback if Taylor is unable to play against Texas this weekend. What started as such an exciting and promising season for Mississippi State may result in a fight just to reach bowl eligibility.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    14. Texas A&M AggiesLast week: 14How many more games will Texas A&M win this season? That's a serious question. The Aggies finish the season with South Carolina (road), Tennessee (home), Oklahoma (road) and Texas (home). Can they get the split necessary just to reach bowl eligibility? Perhaps, but 1-3 seems a lot more likely based on what we've seen from Texas A&M since conference play began all the way back in Week 3. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    15. Arkansas RazorbacksLast week: 15Arkansas got to bask in the glow of its first SEC victory for an extra week due to the open date. Now we'll see whether the Razorbacks can use their win over Vanderbilt as a springboard for the rest of the season. If that's going to happen, KJ Jackson has to take advantage of a Missouri defense that's somewhat vulnerable through the air, allowing 226 passing yards per game. The Hogs are looking to snap a four-game losing streak in that series.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    16. Vanderbilt CommodoresLast week: 16Another week, another loss for the Commodores. That makes five in a row, but Vanderbilt gets a reprieve in the form of an open date. With the exception of Jared Curtis, it's hard to find anything that's working for the Dores these days. Their run game is abysmal coming off a 15-yard showing against Kentucky, and the run defense is getting steamrolled on a regular basis. Clark Lea will have his hands full trying to plug leaks over the next couple of weeks.

        Oregon quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season as he continues to recover from a concussion suffered in September against USC, coach Dan Lanning confirmed on Monday.Moore, one of college football's top signal callers, has several options, including a return to the field in 2027 or declaring for the NFL Draft amid what is expected to be a quarterback-heavy cycle at the top. Moore showed plenty of high-end potential before the injury, and there's no reason to rush back when his future extends well beyond this fall.During such a disastrous campaign for the Ducks, Moore is making the call to shut things down with plenty of runway to re-evaluate what's next. Moore returned to the team this offseason with the expectation that he would help push Oregon back to the College Football Playoff, despite offensive coordinator Will Stein's departure to Kentucky, and believed he had a supporting cast to help achieve that goal.Instead, the Ducks are 4-3 overall and have regressed across all areas, even defensively, where Oregon returned a wealth of talent and added stars in the transfer market. Outside of the CFP conversation after the loss at Illinois, Lanning fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer, who was elevated to the role from within after Stein's departure.
It makes little sense for Moore to jeopardize his development and potential earning power this offseason to trot out there and play during a throwaway home stretch in these final five games.

Moore's eligibility for 2027Under the NCAA's "5-for-5" rule, Moore has another available year of college football left should he choose to play another season for the Ducks or elsewhere next fall. Moore considered opting for the 2026 NFL Draft at the end of his junior season, but announced in January he was returning to Oregon despite projections as a top-5 selection.CBS Sports previously reported that Moore's camp worked through what the quarterback's NIL contract would look like at Oregon this season, as well as an insurance policy in the event of a serious injury that could affect his future draft stock.
Moore assumed additional game experience at Oregon and the opportunity to display more quality film in 2026 for a title contender would push the program -- and his own stock -- to new heights. While the risky decision backfired, it was a calculated move, informed by a thorough assessment from the quarterback and his team.NFL Draft outlookIf Moore declares in a few months and enters the 2027 NFL Draft, he'll be doing so as the No. 45 overall prospect this cycle, per CBS Sports.In our latest first-round mock, Moore is the fifth quarterback projected in the first round at No. 30 overall, a far cry from where he expected to be at the start of the season as the leader of a top-5 team. NFL Draft analyst Josh Edwards notes Moore's "fascinating" decision and how significantly the conversation has shifted for the once-touted prospect. 
"The idea of transferring, falling into another subpar situation and tanking his stock even more is also less than ideal. He may be better off taking his chances in the NFL," Edwards writes.Over three-plus games this season, Moore completed 69.7% of his passes for 926 yards and nine touchdowns without an interception, but did not look as comfortable in Mehringer's system as he did under Stein.What NFL evaluators must determine now is Moore's upside, his long-term health and whether what he's shown over four seasons as a Power Four quarterback warrants Day 1 billing should he declare.
Legacy as former five-star recruitRated as the fourth-best player nationally and the No. 3 quarterback in the 2023 recruiting cycle by 247Sports, Moore's immediate grasp of UCLA's starting quarterback role as a true freshman that season was notable. The Detroit, Michigan, native started the first six games of his college career with 1,610 yards, nine touchdowns and 11 interceptions before he was benched for Ethan Garbers. Moore, a one-time Oregon commit, left the Bruins for the Ducks in the transfer portal after the season as the insurance policy in Eugene behind Oklahoma transfer Dillon Gabriel.Spending that 2024 season behind Gabriel and under the wing of Stein for the Big Ten champions and playoff-bound Ducks was beneficial for Moore, who mastered Oregon's offensive scheme and concepts while waiting his turn.
During his first season as Oregon's starter the following campaign, Moore led the Ducks to 13 wins after finishing with 3,565 passing yards, 30 touchdowns and a 71% completion rate.
